order: Make the guard hook read the session's model before deciding whether to deny a tool call. Today it blocks edit, write, shell, and search tools for every main-session call regardless of which model is running it, so a session already told to go dormant and behave like a plain session is denied every edit anyway, because instructions alone cannot unblock a hook. Read the latest non-sidechain assistant model from the session transcript with a fixed-cost tail read, and enforce only when that model is a director model; any other model stands the guard down entirely. Resolve an undetermined model to enforce, so the harness never silently disappears for an actual director session. Read the latest turn so a mid-session model switch is honored immediately, and skip sidechain entries so a finished scout run under a different model cannot be mistaken for the session's own model. Update the docs to describe the new behavior.
claims: Detection runs only on the would-deny path, so allowed calls pay nothing extra; measured at roughly zero added time over the existing process-spawn cost on an 8.8MB transcript. The guard now reads the latest non-sidechain assistant model before denying, enforcing only for director models and standing down entirely for any other model, with an undetermined model still resolving to enforce. Docs were updated to match.
